source_text.docs/issues/ISS-0276.yaml:
With a fresh dev database, Letflow.Identity.resolve_tenant_by_realm("bpm-default") returns {:error, :not_found} because no tenants row has idp_realm_id = "bpm-default" -- there is no priv/repo/seeds.exs and no dev-bootstrap path that creates one. Only test fixtures (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex) create such a row, and only for the test DB. Discovered live during REQ-116's read-only frontend/API contract sweep (docs/frontend/contract-gaps.md, Environment notes item 2) and worked around live via a throwaway, non-committed script (scratch/bootstrap_tenant.exs, scratch/ is gitignored) that called the real already-shipped lib/ functions directly -- Letflow.Identity.create_tenant/1 -> Letflow.TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 -> Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1, the same three calls Letflow.Routers.Tenants's own POST /tenants handler makes.

Fix direction (from the filing, not binding on CODE-DESIGNER's actual design -- the design step still owns the real approach): add a mix letflow.seed task (or documented bootstrap step) that provisions a default tenant (slug bpm-default, idp_realm_id bpm-default) against a fresh dev database, using the same shipped Identity/TenantProvisioning functions.

Acceptance criteria (for the fix, and thus for the regression test):
1. Running the new seed task/step against a freshly-migrated, empty dev database creates a tenant row with idp_realm_id = "bpm-default".
2. After running it, an authenticated request bearing a valid bpm-default-realm token with a correct aud claim resolves a tenant and proceeds past AuthPipeline's tenant-resolution step.
3. The seed path is documented (README or docs/) so a developer setting up a fresh environment finds it without reading this issue.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for seed/bootstrap/idp_realm_id/resolve_tenant_by_realm/'fresh dev database' -- 25 hits, none resolved for this defect. The one genuinely related record is ISS-0108 (status: open, not resolved) -- a full-suite-only flaky-test issue about test/letflow/identity_test.exs's own private insert_default_tenant!/0 helper (literal slug/realm 'bpm-default') colliding under a suspected sandbox-mode leak; it independently confirms 'bpm-default' is this codebase's established reserved default-tenant slug/realm and that only test-local helpers create such a row today, but its root cause (Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox mode leak between tests) is unrelated to ISS-0276's root cause (no seed path exists at all). VERDICT: first occurrence, not a recurrence -- no prior resolved entry addresses a missing dev-bootstrap/seed task.

STEP 1 (diagnose) -- REPRODUCED LIVE, not source-only. Toolchain and Postgres are reachable in this environment ('/c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix', Mix 1.20.3; docker container e5d38abcb202 'letflow-postgres-1' on host port 5462, matching this checkout's config/db_port.exs default since no LETFLOW_DB_PORT override exists in .env). `mix run scratch/...exs` against the real, persistent, multi-workspace-shared letflow_dev database was refused by an explicit guard in lib/letflow/repo.ex requiring LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 (a real safety measure protecting concurrent workspaces sharing that DB, not a limitation of this environment) -- so reproduction used this project's own documented substitute for exactly this situation instead: an isolated, freshly-created-and-migrated MIX_ENV=test partition (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=999, via `mix ecto.create --quiet` + `mix ecto.migrate --quiet`), which is schema-identical to a fresh dev DB and carries zero seed data, matching the issue's 'freshly-migrated, empty database' scenario exactly. Ran `IO.inspect(Letflow.Identity.resolve_tenant_by_realm("bpm-default"))` via `mix run` against that partition. ACTUAL OUTPUT: `resolve_tenant_by_realm: {:error, :not_found}` (query log: `SELECT ... FROM "tenants" ... WHERE (t0."idp_realm_id" = $1) ["bpm-default"]` returned zero rows) -- confirms the bug reproduces exactly as filed. Partition 999 was dropped afterward (`mix ecto.drop --quiet`) and the throwaway scratch script deleted, leaving no side effects.

ROOT CAUSE (traced to the exact missing code path, confirmed by reading lib/letflow/identity.ex and lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex, not inferred): Letflow.Identity.resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 (lib/letflow/identity.ex:130-135) is a thin, correct `Repo.get_by(Tenant, idp_realm_id: idp_realm_id)` -- it is not itself defective; it faithfully returns {:error, :not_found} because the `tenants` table genuinely has no row with idp_realm_id='bpm-default' on a fresh database. The only code path that could create such a row is Letflow.Identity.create_tenant/1 (identity.ex:582-598, called from Letflow.Routers.Tenants's POST /tenants handler at lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex:225-237, which validates an OPTIONAL `idp_realm_id` field per its @create_schema at lines 198-223) followed by Letflow.TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 (tenant_provisioning.ex:229) and Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1 (tenant_provisioning.ex:303, arity-1 call site -- the 2-arg form takes an optional migration_source, unused by this call chain) -- exactly the three-call chain the issue's own filing already names, confirmed correct against the actual current source. Nothing in this codebase ever calls that chain outside of: (a) an authenticated PLATFORM_ADMIN HTTP request to POST /tenants, (b) test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's provisioned_tenant!/1 (test-only, compiled under elixirc_paths(:test) per mix.exs, uses a random unique_slug and never sets idp_realm_id at all -- confirmed by reading its create_changeset call, identity.ex-style attrs %{slug:, display_name:} with no idp_realm_id key), and (c) test/letflow/identity_test.exs's own private insert_default_tenant!/0 (literal 'bpm-default', test-file-local, not exported/shared). `Glob priv/repo/seeds.exs` returned no match -- the file does not exist -- and `Glob lib/mix/tasks/*.ex` lists six existing custom mix tasks (letflow.copy_identity_tables, letflow.check.test, letflow.check_toolchain, letflow.check_deferral_staleness, letflow.check_requirements_registration, letflow.lint_handoffs), none of which provision a tenant or seed data. So the missing code path is precisely: no `mix letflow.seed` (or equivalently-named) Mix.Task exists anywhere in lib/mix/tasks/, and no dev-bootstrap step is wired into any documented setup flow (README/docs) or run automatically after `mix ecto.migrate` -- a fresh dev database is left with a migrated, empty `tenants` table and no way to reach the three-call provisioning chain except a manual, authenticated HTTP POST that itself requires a PLATFORM_ADMIN-authorized caller, which doesn't exist yet either on a fresh environment.

WHAT A FIX MUST ADD (for CODE-DESIGNER, not implemented here): (1) a new Mix.Task module under lib/mix/tasks/ (naming convention `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Seed` for `mix letflow.seed`, matching the existing `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.*` naming in that directory) that starts the :letflow application/repo the way the existing tasks in that directory do, then calls Letflow.Identity.create_tenant/1 with attrs %{"slug" => "bpm-default", "display_name" => <some default>, "idp_realm_id" => "bpm-default"} (create_tenant/1 expects a caller-validated map with string keys per its @doc and Tenant.create_changeset/3's cast fields -- confirmed against Letflow.Routers.Tenants's own attrs shape at handle_create/1), then Letflow.TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 on the returned tenant.id, then Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1 on the same tenant.id -- the same three calls POST /tenants already makes, per the issue's own fix direction, now confirmed as the only existing call chain that produces a usable tenant row. (2) The task must be idempotent against a database that already has a bpm-default tenant (AC1 only requires it to work on a freshly-migrated, empty database, but CODE-DESIGNER should decide whether re-running is a no-op or an error -- create_tenant/1 already returns {:error, :duplicate_slug} on a second call, which the task should handle explicitly rather than crash on, since developers will plausibly re-run a seed task). (3) CODE-DESIGNER must also account for the LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 guard this run discovered live in lib/letflow/repo.ex: `mix letflow.seed` targets the dev environment by definition, so the design needs to state explicitly whether the seed task must also pass/require that confirmation env var (consistent with every other tool that touches the shared letflow_dev database) or is exempt as a one-time bootstrap action -- this is a real, evidenced constraint from this session's own reproduction attempt, not a hypothetical. (4) AC3 (documentation) needs the new command's invocation documented in README.md or docs/ so a developer setting up a fresh environment finds it -- e.g. alongside the existing `mix ecto.migrate` setup step.

Fix is NOT implemented in this step, per WF-03 Step 1 and this handoff's task.description.
